item.title: Iran’s Naval Mines: A History of Threats to Persian Gulf Shipping
item.summary: The U.S. said this week that it attacked 16 Iranian mine-laying vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. In the 1980s, Iranian mines damaged oil tankers and a U.S. Navy warship.

item.title: How Hegseth Came to See Moral Purpose in War as Weakness
item.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s bellicose and vengeful rhetoric describing the military’s war in Iran grew out of his experience in Iraq.

item.title: Deadly Attack on Oil Tankers Prompts Iraq to Close Oil Terminals
item.summary: An attack off the Iraqi coast engulfed two oil tankers in flames, killing at least one person. Senior Iraqi officials believe the attack was Iranian.

item.title: Israel Bombards Lebanese Capital in Latest Round of Strikes
item.summary: Lebanon’s health ministry said at least seven people were killed in the Beirut attacks early Thursday.

item.title: U.N. Security Council Condemns Iran’s Retaliatory Strikes in the Middle East
item.summary: In an overwhelming vote, the council backed a resolution condemning Iran. A Russian proposal calling for an end to the war that didn’t assign blame or even name the parties, was rejected.

item.title: Countries Scramble to Shore Up Global Oil Supplies as Ships Are Attacked
item.summary: The United States and Israel launched more strikes against Iran, where crowds mourned military commanders killed in the war. Israel also bombed targets in Lebanon, where the death toll climbed.

item.title: California Officials See No Imminent Threat of Drone Attacks by Iran
item.summary: Just before the war began, the Federal Bureau of Investigation told state officials that Iran might respond with drone attacks on California. No specific, credible threats have been identified.

item.title: What Happened in the U.S.-Israeli War on Iran on Wednesday
item.summary: Israel and the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah in Lebanon traded strikes on Wednesday. Three ships were hit near the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil route.

item.title: First Week of Iran War Cost More Than $11 Billion, Pentagon Tells Congress
item.summary: In a Capitol Hill briefing, officials gave their most comprehensive assessment of the cost of the first six days of the war, but the number omitted several aspects of the operation.

item.title: Banks in Gulf Evacuate Their Offices
item.summary: After an overnight attack on a bank, Iranian officials signaled a new willingness to target economic centers and banks with ties to the United States.
